questions.question: Q: Explain two Christian beliefs about the afterlife.

points.text: 1) Resurrection — Christians believe that, like Jesus, the dead will be raised to new life. This is a physical resurrection, not just spiritual survival. 2) Judgement — Christians believe God will judge all people, as described in the parable of the sheep and goats (Matthew 25). Those who have lived according to God's will enter eternal life; those who have rejected God face separation.

questions.question: Q: "Belief in the afterlife gives life meaning." Evaluate this statement.

points.text: Many Christians would agree — without belief in eternal life, earthly existence could seem pointless. The afterlife gives meaning to suffering, motivates moral behaviour, and provides comfort. However, some argue that meaning can be found in this life alone through relationships, achievement and contribution to society. Atheists and humanists find meaning without afterlife beliefs.
